turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Kia ora, thanks for calling Acme, you're speaking with Sam. Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. How can I help today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh, hello. Yes. I saw your... the advert, on the telly. About life cover. I wanted to ask about it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No worries at all, happy to help with that. Before I go into any of your details or a quote, can I just confirm your full name and date of birth please?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Sorry, my name and...?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Your full name and your date of birth.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. Oliver James Brown. And it's the... fourteenth of March, nineteen sixty-one.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks Oliver, that's all confirmed. So to make sure we look at the right thing for you, can you tell me a bit about your situation and why you're thinking about life cover?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Well. I had a stroke, about... eight months ago now. I'm doing better but my words still get muddled sometimes, and I lose track. My wife, Helen, she's worried. If something happened, I'd want her to be alright. With the mortgage and that.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Sorry to hear about the stroke, glad you're on the mend. How much is left on the mortgage, roughly, and is there anyone else who depends on you financially?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: About... two hundred and forty thousand, I think. The kids are grown up. It's just Helen and me.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great, that helps. And are you still working at the moment, or retired?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I stopped working after the stroke. Helen still works part-time.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay, thanks. So based on that, something around the mortgage amount makes sense. Acme Life Cover lets you choose a cover amount anywhere from fifty thousand up to one million dollars, so two hundred and fifty thousand would clear the mortgage with a bit left over. Premiums are stepped, which means they go up each year as you get older. There's also a terminal illness benefit, so if you were diagnosed with less than twelve months to live, it pays out early. Now the important one for you: pre-existing medical conditions aren't covered for the first two years, so anything related to the stroke wouldn't be covered in that period.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Sorry, can you say that again? The bit about... the steps?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Sure, stepped premiums, so the price goes up every year as you get older. And the stroke counts as a pre-existing condition, so it isn't covered for the first two years. For a two hundred and fifty thousand dollar cover amount at your age, the starting premium would be around one hundred and eighty-six dollars a month, and that would increase each year.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: One hundred and... eighty?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: One eighty-six a month to start. Then it steps up each year. You also get a thirty-day free-look period, so if you take it out and change your mind within thirty days, you get a full refund.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I'm sorry, it's a lot at once. My head gets... it gets foggy. So if I, if I died from the stroke, Helen wouldn't get it?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Not in the first two years, no, because that's linked to the pre-existing condition. After two years it would be covered. Anything unrelated to the stroke, like an accident, would be covered from the start, subject to the policy terms.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Two years. Right. And the price goes up.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's it, each year. If you wanted, we could also look at a lower cover amount, say one fifty thousand, which would bring the starting premium down to about one hundred and twelve a month. Or we could go up to three hundred thousand if you wanted extra for Helen beyond the mortgage, that'd be roughly two twenty-three a month to start.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hang on. Which one was the... the hundred and twelve?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's one hundred and fifty thousand of cover. Two fifty is one eighty-six, three hundred is two twenty-three. All monthly, all stepped. And the terminal illness benefit and the free-look apply whichever one you pick.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Mm. I wrote down... I've got one eighty-six here. I think. Sorry, I don't think I'm keeping up very well.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's fine. So the main things are the cover amount, the stepped premium, the two-year wait on the stroke, and the thirty-day free-look. If you're happy with two fifty, I can take you through the application questions now, it takes about fifteen minutes.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Fifteen minutes. Hmm. I don't know. I think I'd like Helen to hear all this. She's better with the numbers than me now.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Of course, that's completely up to you. There's no rush on our side, the cover's available whenever you're ready.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Could you, um, could you send me something? In writing?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Yes, I can email you a summary of the quote and the policy document. What's the best email address for you?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: It's oliver dot brown sixty-one at xtra dot co dot nz.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Lovely, I'll send the quotes for one fifty, two fifty and three hundred thousand through today, along with the policy wording. You and Helen can go through it together and give us a call back on the same number whenever suits.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. Yes. I think that's best. I won't decide today.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No problem at all, Oliver. Is there anything else I can help with today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, I don't think so. Thank you, Sam.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks for calling, Oliver. Take care and all the best with your recovery. Ka kite.
